title: Utah Pterodactyl Report Surfaces in 2010 UFO File
excerpt: A 2010 government file describes witnesses who reported a giant bird with a 12-foot wingspan near Fort Duchesne, Utah.
content:
Live Poll

Do you trust viral videos of unexplained creatures shared on social media?

A 60-page Utah investigation prepared by Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies, released in a 2010 UFO file, recorded witness accounts of a pterodactyl-like creature. The report did not identify the animal, and witnesses said no attack occurred during the encounter.

Why it matters

The account resurfaced alongside videos of a winged silhouette shared by Mexican UFO commentator Jaime Maussan, prompting renewed interest in unexplained sightings in the region. Fact-checkers have rejected claims that the Mexican footage proves a living pterosaur was filmed, leaving the Utah accounts unexplained.

The players

Jaime Maussan

Mexican UFO commentator who shared videos of a winged silhouette filmed over Ciudad Juárez.

Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies

Research division that prepared the 60-page Utah investigation report included in the 2010 UFO file.

The details

Two witnesses reported spotting a giant bird after playing basketball, saying they heard wings flapping and saw branches move as the figure descended toward nearby trees. They ran indoors because they feared the figure was large enough to carry them away.

Timeline

  1. Summer 2006 or 2007: Utah witnesses reported the encounter.

  2. 22 to 26 March 2010: Bigelow Aerospace team first visited the Utah area.

  3. 19 to 23 April 2010: Bigelow Aerospace team returned to the Utah area.

  4. 7 November 2026: Interestelar recording reportedly filmed in the Felipe Ángeles neighbourhood.

  5. 11 November 2026: Jaime Maussan shared the Juárez clip on X.

Wildlife Context

The Utah account revisits a 2010 government UFO file that documented witness testimony rather than physical evidence of an animal. It sits alongside the 2026 Mexican footage, which fact-checkers have rejected as proof of a living pterosaur.

Reports like this one are based on witness testimony gathered during investigations, not confirmed physical specimens. Readers weighing claims about unusual animal sightings should look for independent verification before drawing conclusions.

The takeaway

Witness testimony can prompt investigation but does not by itself establish what was seen. Checking claims against independent evidence and fact-checks helps separate documented accounts from confirmed findings.
